content: Fenofibrate is a medication prescribed to help reduce levels of cholesterol and triglycerides (types of fats) in the blood. It is used in conjunction with dietary changes that limit the intake of cholesterol and fats. High levels of cholesterol and triglycerides can lead to the buildup of fatty deposits along the walls of arteries, a condition called atherosclerosis. This can restrict blood flow and reduce oxygen delivery to vital organs such as the heart and brain. By lowering these levels, fenofibrate may help prevent cardiovascular diseases, including heart disease, angina (chest pain), strokes, and heart attacks. If you have questions about other potential uses of this medication, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Fenofibrate is available in capsule form and is taken orally, typically once daily with a meal. It is important to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any doubts or need clarification, ask your doctor or pharmacist. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Even if you feel well, continue taking fenofibrate unless directed otherwise by your doctor. Do not stop taking it without consulting your healthcare provider. Before starting fenofibrate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to fenofibrate or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs you are taking, especially anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), cholesterol-lowering medications (e.g., lovastatin, pravastatin, simvastatin), cholestyramine, cyclosporine, vitamins, or herbal supplements. Additionally, disclose if you have a history of heart disease, gallbladder disease, liver disease, or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking fenofibrate, contact your doctor immediately. While taking fenofibrate, adhere to a low-cholesterol, low-fat diet. This diet should include foods such as cottage cheese, fat-free milk, fish, vegetables, poultry, egg whites, and polyunsaturated oils or margarines (e.g., corn, safflower, canola, soybean oils). Avoid high-fat foods, including fatty meats, liver, egg yolks, whole milk, cream, butter, shortening, pastries, cakes, cookies, gravy, peanut butter, chocolate, olives, potato chips, coconut, cheese (except cottage cheese), coconut oil, palm oil, and fried foods. If you miss a dose of fenofibrate, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Fenofibrate may cause side effects. Minor side effects include gas, headache, stomach pain, upset stomach, dizziness, lightheadedness, constipation, fatigue, and a runny nose. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, which require immediate medical attention, include muscle pain or tenderness, weakness, joint pain, rash, infection, or flu-like symptoms. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store fenofibrate in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. It is important to keep all appointments with your doctor and undergo any recommended laboratory tests to monitor your response to fenofibrate. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Fenofibrate is sold under brand names such as Lofibra and TriCor.
